questions.topic: Main-Content Extraction and Boilerplate Removal
questions.question: What is the goal of main-content extraction?
options: Retaining the primary semantic content while removing repeated site chrome
Recovering scripts and inline styles so their text becomes searchable prose
Flattening the whole DOM into one string, ignoring rendered visibility rules
Rewriting article prose using the anchor labels found in the navigation tree

questions.topic: Main-Content Extraction and Boilerplate Removal
questions.question: Which feature often indicates navigation boilerplate?
options: Long sentences with low link density spread over several paragraphs
Many short anchor texts packed into a block with high link density
A central article element holding headings and paragraph-length prose
Code blocks sitting beneath descriptive headings inside a main region

questions.topic: Main-Content Extraction and Boilerplate Removal
questions.question: Why can indexing full body text damage retrieval?
options: Navigation terms appear on only one page each, so they become far too rare
Article prose is dropped by the tokenizer before any postings are written
Repeated chrome inflates document frequency and creates duplicate chunks
The DOM cannot hold links and paragraphs together, so one set is discarded

questions.topic: Main-Content Extraction and Boilerplate Removal
questions.question: Fetched text says only Enable JavaScript to continue, while the page should contain a guide. What should happen?
options: Mark extraction as successful, since the parser returned a nonempty string
Index the shell phrase as the guide, since it is the only text the page returned
Discard the raw artifact and its provenance so the URL is never refetched
Trigger a rendered fallback or quarantine, since shell text signals failure

questions.topic: Main-Content Extraction and Boilerplate Removal
questions.question: Why is repeated text not always safe to remove?
options: A safety notice or version banner repeated site-wide can be essential context
Repetition across a site is reliable proof that the region is advertising markup
Template learning cannot identify DOM paths that recur across many pages
Repeated regions never contribute tokens that a downstream answer would use

questions.topic: Main-Content Extraction and Boilerplate Removal
questions.question: Why preserve raw artifact hashes after extraction?
options: They certify that the extracted text is semantically faithful to the source
Better parsers can reprocess the identical source bytes without refetching
They remove the need to record the extractor version alongside the output
They allow every removed DOM node to be reconstructed from the hash alone

questions.topic: HTML to Clean Text: Which Structure to Preserve
questions.question: Which HTML relationship should clean text preserve?
options: The execution order of the tracking scripts embedded in the page head
The animation timing declared for the cookie banner and its buttons
The heading hierarchy and the paragraph and list boundaries under it
The CSS colour values applied to decorative icons beside each heading

questions.topic: HTML to Clean Text: Which Structure to Preserve
questions.question: Why should table headers remain associated with cells?
options: Headers force every row of the table to repeat the same set of values
Headers are decorative markup and can be dropped along with the styling rules
Cell order alone is enough to recover each value's unit and dimension
A value detached from its row and column no longer states what it measures

questions.topic: HTML to Clean Text: Which Structure to Preserve
questions.question: How should an inline code value such as 100 be represented?
options: Keep its code semantics rather than flattening it into ordinary prose
Drop the value, since bare numeric tokens carry no retrievable meaning
Render it as an image so the original monospaced styling is preserved
Repeat it once per CSS class on the element so weighting reflects markup

questions.topic: HTML to Clean Text: Which Structure to Preserve
questions.question: Why emit a deterministic normalized-content hash?
options: It proves that two pages with different hashes carry different meanings
It shows when output changed, so downstream chunks can be invalidated
It stands in for the URL, fetch time, and extractor version provenance
It forces successive parser versions to produce byte-identical output

questions.topic: HTML to Clean Text: Which Structure to Preserve
questions.question: A complex table has merged cells that Markdown cannot represent faithfully. What is the best response?
options: Flatten every cell into one sentence and drop the header row entirely
Discard the table, since no downstream task can use merged-cell data
Keep the HTML or a structured record that retains the cell relationships
Sort the cells alphabetically so the extractor output stays deterministic

questions.topic: HTML to Clean Text: Which Structure to Preserve
questions.question: How should structure preservation vary by downstream task?
options: Deliver one structureless string, since every task tokenizes it anyway
Give bag-of-words retrieval more layout than table question answering
Normalize whitespace and syntax away, since code retrieval matches tokens
Preserve the minimum reversible structure the declared features require

questions.topic: Extracting Text from PDFs and Office Documents
questions.question: Why is PDF text extraction fundamentally difficult?
options: PDF stores positioned glyphs and may carry no semantic reading order
PDF always exposes a clean paragraph tree that parsers must re-flatten
Every PDF page ships an OCR transcript that overrides the glyph layer
PDF cannot represent tables, images, or multi-column page layouts

questions.topic: Extracting Text from PDFs and Office Documents
questions.question: When is OCR required?
options: Whenever the file is a PDF, since glyph coordinates cannot be parsed
When the pages are scans carrying no usable embedded text layer
Whenever a DOCX package contains headings, tables, or footnotes
Whenever a spreadsheet stores formulas alongside cached values

questions.topic: Extracting Text from PDFs and Office Documents
questions.question: What can happen if a two-column PDF is sorted only by vertical coordinate?
options: The two columns are split into separate documents with their own page order
Repeated page headers and footers are stripped away along with the columns
Lines from the left and right columns interleave into unreadable prose
Every glyph is assigned a paragraph label derived from its font metrics

questions.topic: Extracting Text from PDFs and Office Documents
questions.question: A spreadsheet cell contains formula A2 times 1.1 and displayed value 110. What should extraction decide explicitly?
options: Whether the sheet name and cell coordinates are worth storing at all
Whether external macros should be executed to refresh the cached value
Whether each formula should be rendered as an image of the formula bar
Whether the corpus needs the formula, the value, or both with headers

questions.topic: Extracting Text from PDFs and Office Documents
questions.question: Why should document parsing run in isolated resource-limited workers?
options: Files can carry macros, decompression bombs, and parser-exploiting objects
Isolation raises OCR accuracy by giving each page a dedicated recognizer
Office packages cannot be opened at all without executing their macros
Resource caps convert complex page layouts into simple linear text runs

questions.topic: Extracting Text from PDFs and Office Documents
questions.question: Why is an apparently empty PDF not immediately discardable?
options: Empty PDFs still carry the document text inside their filename metadata
It may be a scanned document needing OCR rather than text-layer parsing
An empty text layer is direct proof that the visual pages are blank
Every PDF hides a spreadsheet object that a format-aware parser can read

questions.topic: Extraction Quality Judgments: When to Discard a Document
questions.question: Which signal directly measures extraction character corruption?
options: The number of HTTP redirects followed before the artifact was fetched
The frontier priority score assigned to the URL at discovery time
The share of replacement characters in the normalized extracted text
The rank the source page held in the search API result that found it

questions.topic: Extraction Quality Judgments: When to Discard a Document
questions.question: What are the four useful routing outcomes for extraction quality?
options: Fetch the bytes, rank the text, generate an answer, then bill the tenant
Accept the text, index it, publish the document, then forget the source
Parse the file, render the pages, tokenize the text, then embed the chunks
Accept, retry with a fallback parser, quarantine for review, or discard

questions.topic: Extraction Quality Judgments: When to Discard a Document
questions.question: A 20-page PDF yields 25 words, 15% replacement characters, and only two processed pages. What is appropriate?
options: Fail automatic acceptance and route it to a fallback parser or quarantine
Accept it, since a nonempty string is enough for downstream chunking
Treat the low yield as evidence that the original document is short
Publish it beside verified extractions, since the parser reported no error

questions.topic: Extraction Quality Judgments: When to Discard a Document
questions.question: Why should discard decisions retain reason codes and attempts?
options: So the source can never be reprocessed once the decision is recorded
So the source is not reacquired endlessly and lineage stays auditable
So every discarded artifact can be classified as malicious by default
So source-specific quality thresholds become unnecessary to maintain

questions.topic: Extraction Quality Judgments: When to Discard a Document
questions.question: Why is one global minimum token count a poor quality rule?
options: Token counts cannot be computed until chunking and embedding have run
Valid documents of every type share one expected length distribution
A two-line notice is valid while a manual with that yield is broken
A single threshold already reflects parser warnings and page coverage

questions.topic: Extraction Quality Judgments: When to Discard a Document
questions.question: How should a required compliance contract with uncertain extraction be handled?
options: Discard it quietly, applying the same policy a broad web corpus uses
Index the corrupted text without a quality marker so nothing is lost
Delete the raw artifact so a later review cannot surface the failure
Quarantine it and raise an alert instead of losing required content
